items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: it’s John Bunch and Jay Leonhart, just a trio... We played, I remember we played about three weeks, three or four weeks. And it was a great rhythm section.

ctx.x: And these days, you split your time between going around to these jazz parties and doing recording. Have you got a recording session planned coming up?

No the only records we make now for companies that want to make a jazz record like Arbors or the company I used to be with, LRC Records with New York Swing, it’s John Bunch and Jay Leonhart, just a trio, and then we add drums, either Bernard Purdie or Dennis Mackrel or Joe Cocuzzo. But we found out that it works better on the road with just three, without the drums.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And then the week before we did something with John Bunch doing all Tony Bennett songs, and mostly all piano and I just played rhythm behind them.

ctx.x: Your kids have done well for themselves. I’m wondering if you’ve gotten to the point where you learn anything from them?

Oh yeah. Yeah. They come up with some good stuff. Tunes — I know John is about to make an album. He does a lot of research on it. I used to tell him listen to this guy, listen to that guy. He does a great rendition of a certain tune you ought to look into. That’s all. That’s as far as it goes. But he’s got a hot trio. They’re very good.
Yeah. He’s got a good personality on stage.
